premise.claim: On the merge-base, ServiceReconciler.reconcileHeadlessService re-reads the workload through the cached (informer-backed) client immediately after the same reconcile pass created/applied it. When the informer cache has not yet observed the write, the Get returns NotFound, the whole RoleBasedGroup role reconcile errors, and the headless Service is only created on a later retry. PR body: 'Reuse the workload object returned by the API server when reconciling the headless Service, instead of reading the workload from the informer cache immediately after creating or applying it.'
premise.patchedComponent: pkg/reconciler/svc_reconciler.go (reconcileHeadlessService now takes the workload; getObjectByKind deleted), pkg/reconciler/roleinstanceset_reconciler.go, pkg/reconciler/sts_reconciler.go, pkg/utils/utils.go (ApplyObjectConfiguration returns the server response)
premise.evidence: results/base-premise.out — the contract test grafted onto merge-base 1fc69f703 fails with 'roleinstancesets.workloads.x-k8s.io "group-worker" not found' from the lagging-cache Get inside reconcileHeadlessService; the identical test passes on the PR head (results/head-harness.out) with the headless Service created and the correct ownerRef UID.
match: contract: reconcile must not fail because the informer cache lags the workload write

liveNote: L3 (live cluster) not run this round: the claim is decided at the controller/client layer, which envtest exercises with a real API server. The informer-cache lag the PR fixes is deterministic in the harness's laggingCacheClient; a live run would only re-demonstrate the same NotFound retry. If a live check is wanted, deploy a controller built from the PR head and confirm the first reconcile of a fresh RBG creates the headless Service without a 'not found' Reconciler error in the logs.
